name: module-fqn-prefix
body:
The module identity that prefixes a module's symbol FQNs. Several distinct meanings share the one Module namespace, and they must stay collision-free because the ingestor panics on a residual Module FQN collision rather than overwriting (SPEC §4).

(1) Discovered code projects — language/package-derived: a Cargo package name (root `apg` vs nested `apg-rustfrontend`) or an npm package name for JS/TS. Distinct prefixes keep nested-project FQNs disjoint (see requirements.requirement.rust-nested-fqn-clean).

(2) Markdown documents — path-derived: a markdown Module's FQN is its directory's absolute path, and its File's FQN is the file's absolute path with the extension retained (`docs/README.md` and `docs/README.markdown` stay distinct). This is the pinned scheme (requirements.requirement.markdown-sections-as-symbols, requirements.requirement.markdown-accept-extensions), NOT the rejected dot-joined directory scheme, which is lossy (it aliases `docs/guide` and `docs.guide` to the same `docs.guide` prefix).

(3) Repo-root markdown directory — the repo-root directory's absolute path. The root directory is itself a directory with an absolute path, so there is always a path to name it; this closes open point 5 of requirements.note.markdown-frontend-open-points, whose premise that the root directory offers no path to name it was wrong.

(4) Python packages — package-derived dotted identity: a directory with __init__.py/__init__.pyi is a package, and the dotted identity walks up init-bearing ancestors; a file with no init-bearing ancestor is a flat top-level module by stem (domain.entity.python-package, requirements.requirement.python-package-identity). Like (1) this is a language/package-derived identity, so it is NOT automatically disjoint from other languages' module names — a root Python package `apg` would render the same Module FQN as the Rust `apg` module, and two same-stem init-less top-level modules in different directories would alias. python-package-identity therefore requires collision-freedom across the whole scan; the namespace form that guarantees it (bare dotted, a path-derived absolute-path form like (2), or a language-namespaced form) is an open design point (requirements.note.python-frontend-open-points).

Collision hazard and resolution: a markdown Module FQN (a directory's absolute path) and a code Module FQN (a language/package-derived name) both live in the one Module namespace, so any scheme that named the root markdown module by its directory basename or a dot-joined path could alias a code module name. The absolute-path construction rules that out: a POSIX absolute path begins with `/`, which no Cargo package name, npm package name, Go module path, or Java/other package name does, so the repo-root markdown Module (the repo-root absolute path) can never collide with the existing `apg` Rust module. Path-derived identities are thus disjoint from language/package-derived identities by construction, and module/file prefixes stay disjoint because absolute paths are unique per directory and per file. The Python package identity (4) is language/package-derived and so does not inherit that guarantee; it needs its own collision-free namespace form (open point).
